statement_summary: One CSF 2.0 program covering IT and OT for every division
Named accountable roles, including RRA and ERP manager, CMMC Affirming Official, and hazmat plan senior official
Annual SP 800-30 risk analysis per division with roll-up; RRA cyber element from inventory and register
Risk acceptance authority by level; public health and worker safety High risks must be treated
Division supplements may not weaken group policy; re-align within 90 days; annual attestation
Divisions document inherited common controls every year
Sanctions for policy violations
Supplier security terms, including for sister divisions acting as suppliers
Annual common control assessment and division samples; review before any government self-assessment or affirmation
Written, time-limited exceptions; OT remote access exceptions need the Group OT Security Director
Retention: 6 years for security records; RRAs and ERPs 5 years after certification
AI systems registered and approved under the Group AI Standard
Named accounts; no shared accounts except staffed control-room shift sessions with named sign-in
Least privilege with HMI roles
MFA for remote, privileged, and cloud access; phishing-resistant for administrators
OT remote access only through SYS-G4 with MFA, per-session approval, recording, and weekly review; no exceptions to approval
Access removed within 4 hours of termination
Quarterly certification of IT, OT, and gateway accounts; monthly for privileged
Privileged access through PAM; no standing local administrator rights on engineering workstations
Default credentials changed before devices enter service
Break-glass accounts sealed, monitored, rotated after use
Non-owned devices connect to OT only on maintenance segments under an interconnection agreement
Covered defense information accessed only inside SYS-C2
Report within 1 hour; operators act on process safety first
One severity scale and group playbooks including the OT playbook
Record when each regulated clock starts
Tier 1 notice and primacy consultation decisions within 24 hours; public health notices never wait for legal review
DFARS 72-hour report, DC3 malware submission, 90-day preservation, two certificate holders
Counsel owns the matrix; reviews quarterly; approves legal notices
regulatory_driver: State breach laws; SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05

statement_summary: Severity 1 to the disclosure committee within 24 hours; Form 8-K within 4 business days of a materiality determination
Ransom payment approvals and OFAC sanctions check
Annual cross-division exercise with an OT scenario, the matrix, and a materiality decision
Evidence preservation without delaying safety actions
Lessons learned within 30 days; update registers, POA&M, and ERPs
Owner assigns a class to every dataset
CUI only in SYS-C2; no laptops, removable media, or SYS-C1; FIPS-validated transfer
Critical infrastructure records in restricted repositories; RRA and ERP retention
Encryption at rest and in transit for Restricted and Confidential data
FCI tenants tagged on SYS-E1
Client data used only for the client's service; deleted within 60 days of contract end
Offline OT backups monthly and after change; immutable cloud backups
Media sanitization; consumer report disposal
Retention per records schedule
No personal devices on OT or the CUI enclave
Removable media on OT only after scanning; never for CUI
Report phishing and unexplained HMI behavior at once
Approved AI tools only; no CUI, FCI, RRA content, or client data in unapproved tools
Commissioning and technician laptops stay managed and hold no CUI
